chosen.premise: Six Exeggcute together form one full-fledged Pokémon, and a missing member is replaced by the next morning.
chosen.hook: Six eggs don’t make a team—they make one Pokémon.
chosen.visualIdea: Label six separate eggs as one creature, remove one, then reveal a restored six-member cluster at sunrise.
chosen.note: The strongest premise: six apparent individuals are literally one Pokémon, and a missing member is replaced by morning. It is concrete, bizarre, highly visual, and directly backed by the entries.

candidates.premise: Exeggcute must have exactly six heads to stay balanced, with the cluster attracting and spinning around.
candidates.hook: Exeggcute isn’t one egg—it needs six heads just to balance.
candidates.visualIdea: Show six egg heads locking into a spinning formation, then remove one and tip the cluster sideways.
candidates.note: A highly Exeggcute-specific physical rule with clear animation potential. The six-head requirement and spinning balance are directly supported.

candidates.premise: If one Exeggcute separates, the energy bond between all six instantly pulls it back into the cluster.
candidates.hook: Try separating one Exeggcute—the others will pull it back instantly.
candidates.visualIdea: Stretch one head away from the group with an energy tether, then snap it back into formation.
candidates.note: The instant rejoining is distinctive and strongly supported, though the energy-tether visual is an interpretation rather than something explicitly depicted.

candidates.premise: Cracks signal that Exeggcute is nearing evolution, yet its durable shells let it survive without spilling their contents.
candidates.hook: For Exeggcute, cracking open is actually a sign of evolution.
candidates.visualIdea: Zoom into growing shell cracks, then transition the six-head cluster into Exeggutor after a Leaf Stone.
candidates.note: Excellent contradiction and transformation hook. The entries say increasing cracks mean evolution is near, but do not establish that cracking causes evolution; the Leaf Stone connection is supported separately.

candidates.premise: Exeggcute looks like six eggs, but research identifies it as a life-form more like plant seeds.
candidates.hook: Those eggs aren’t eggs—they’re closer to plant seeds.
candidates.visualIdea: Begin with an egg carton, reveal six faces, then crack the illusion into seeds with plant roots.
candidates.note: The egg-versus-seed contradiction is well supported and easy to visualize, but the basic reveal is familiar to knowledgeable fans.

candidates.premise: Alolan Exeggcute are the same size as others but much heavier because their shells are packed full.
candidates.hook: Alolan Exeggcute are the same size—but much heavier.
candidates.visualIdea: Place standard and Alolan six-egg clusters side by side at the same size, then make the Alolan one drop a scale.
candidates.note: A precise same-size-but-heavier comparison with solid support. It loses visual strength because the research provides no Alolan artwork or exact weight comparison.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is necessary from the supplied research; the episode should center on the rule that six eggs form one Pokémon and the group is restored by the next morning.
